findings.title: Destructuring empty destinationCalendar array then dereferencing causes TypeError
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` dereferences `undefined` whenever `destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array (common: user/event type with no destination calendar). Since `handleNewBooking` can now pass `null`, any booking whose location is Google Meet without a destination calendar will throw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and the booking fails. Use optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`).

findings.title: Video booking references lose credentialId
findings.body: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the credentialId for non-calendar (video) results, whereas the previous code used `result.credentialId` for them. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so newly created bookings will no longer have their video meetings cancelled/updated. Keep `result.credentialId` for the non-calendar branch.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback lookup is logically impossible
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — the `find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals `undefined`/`""` and always returns undefined. The previous code fell back to the event's destination calendar externalId. Consequence: updates without an explicit externalCalendarId are sent with `calendarId: undefined` (API error), and deletes silently fall back to `"primary"`, leaving events in other calendars. Same bug at line 317 in `deleteEvent`.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services ignore credentialId and always use the first destination calendar
findings.body: `createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates every destination calendar and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` with the full multi-entry `event.destinationCalendar`. Only GoogleCalendarService selects the entry matching `credentialId`; Office365 (here), Lark and the CalDAV base service take `destinationCalendar[0]`. For a collective event with hosts on different accounts, each host's credential will attempt to write into the first host's calendar id, producing 404/permission errors or duplicate events in the wrong calendar. These services need the credentialId-aware selection too.

findings.title: Team destination calendars are dropped when there is no event-type/organizer calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and then `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op. Collective hosts' calendars are silently discarded in that case — exactly the scenario this PR aims to fix. Initialize to an array before pushing.

findings.title: loadUsers rewrite drops organization select and changes error semantics
findings.body: The rewritten dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`, which downstream code (org-aware booker URLs / org slug resolution) relies on, so dynamic group bookings for org users may lose organization context. Additionally, the thrown plain `Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is neither `HttpError` nor a Prisma error, so it is converted to a 500 instead of the former 400-style validation failure.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation now deletes each event once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring-cancellation block (iterating all user calendar credentials × all updatedBookings) is now nested inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references the same delete calls are issued N times per booking occurrence, multiplying external API calls and producing repeated 404/410 responses. The recurring branch should be executed once, outside the per-reference loop.

findings.title: updateEvent called with possibly undefined credential
findings.body: After the DB lookup, `credential` can still be undefined (credential missing or `app.slug` null), yet `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId))` is executed unconditionally. `updateEvent` immediately reads `credential.appName`/`credential.id`, so this throws inside the try block and the whole update is reported as failed for all references. Guard with `if (credential)` as the create path does.

findings.title: Organization slug assignment logic inverted (unrelated to this PR)
findings.body: Changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This inverts behavior: with billing enabled the org now gets a real `slug` immediately (bypassing the pending `requestedSlug` flow, and setting both at once), and with billing disabled the org is created with no slug at all, breaking org subdomain resolution. This change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar fix and looks accidental.

findings.title: Inconsistent expected destinationCalendar across webhook tests
findings.body: BOOKING_REJECTED now expects `destinationCalendar: []` while BOOKING_CREATED (line 119) and BOOKING_REQUESTED (line 373) still expect `null`. The payload shape is now an array-or-null depending on the code path, which indicates the API contract is inconsistent for webhook consumers; it should be normalized (always array) and the tests updated accordingly.
